If those 20 points were fixes that simply maintained existing adapter behavior, keep them out of the **modernization progress numerator**. They supported operations, not the new capability milestone.

But “debt work doesn’t move us forward” is too broad. Retiring a legacy dependency, moving an adapter onto the new platform, or removing a migration blocker can be modernization progress—even without a new feature.

The scorecard rule should be:

> **Count work that demonstrably advances an agreed modernization milestone, regardless of whether it’s labeled feature, fix, or debt. Report maintenance separately.**

For this sprint, assuming your descriptions hold:
- **Modernization delivery:** 40 points.
- **Legacy maintenance:** 20 points.
- **Total delivered:** 60 points.

One important distinction: **story points show effort, not client milestone progress.** The client-facing metric should emphasize accepted capabilities, completed migrations, or retired legacy components. The 40 points can support that story, but don’t establish it.

So: keep the patching out of the progress numerator, but visible in the capacity breakdown. That gives the client a clean progress signal without hiding the cost of keeping the old hull afloat.

## Executive Milestone Audit Memo

**Subject:** Sprint modernization achievement and amended Phase 2 milestone scope  
**Basis:** Management’s description of sprint delivery and the signed SOW amendment; underlying documentation has not been independently reviewed.

### Determination

**Report 40 points in the modernization achievement metric and exclude the 20 adapter-fix points from that metric.** This treatment reflects the reported nature of the adapter work: maintaining existing functionality rather than delivering a new platform capability or otherwise advancing technical modernization.

The 20 adapter points remain part of total sprint delivery and, under the amendment as described, are included in Phase 2 contractual milestone scope. Their exclusion from the modernization achievement metric does **not** determine their eligibility for payment.

### Rationale

The modernization achievement metric should count work that demonstrably advances an agreed technical modernization outcome, regardless of whether it is labeled feature, fix, or debt.

A contractual amendment can change milestone scope and payment eligibility. It does not, by itself, demonstrate a change in technical capability. On the facts provided, the adapter work continued to serve a maintenance function; no distinct modernization outcome has been identified for those 20 points.

Accordingly, contractual milestone reporting and technical modernization reporting require separate treatment.

### Scorecard treatment

| Measure | Sprint treatment |
|---|---|
| Total delivery | 60 points |
| Delivery attributed to modernization achievement | 40 feature points |
| Legacy maintenance excluded from modernization achievement | 20 adapter-fix points |
| Contractual milestone credit | Apply the amended SOW’s scope, acceptance criteria, and payout provisions, including the adapter work |

Story points represent delivery effort, not an independent measure of capability achieved. The modernization entry should therefore be supported by evidence of the associated technical outcomes.

### Executive disclosure

> Sprint delivery totaled 60 points. Of these, 40 are attributed to modernization achievement and 20 to maintenance of existing adapter functionality. The signed SOW amendment includes the adapter work in Phase 2 contractual milestone scope; this changes its contractual treatment but does not, on the evidence described, establish additional technical modernization achievement.

If subsequent evidence demonstrates that the adapter work delivered a qualifying modernization outcome, its technical classification should be reassessed on that evidence—not on the payout designation alone.
